Harder than heck

This tune is tough, I’ve seen it transposed in all different settings, keys etc. but this is the setting I was taught. In internet land it also seems to be the rarest - good going AC!! crackin’ tune

↳ Posted by b.maloney on January 30th, 2002.

The B-Parts a little different from what I play, I play it as follows:

abga fece|fbba geea|gebe c‘ebe|ac’ea c‘ae’c’|
abga fece|dcBc defg|(3aba gb afec|1 dcBe cAAg:|2 dcBe cAA2||

You need to go into the 2nd position for this one, this was my 2nd position lesson.

The Dawn - De Dannan version

I lost the album that had “The Dawn” on it by De Dannan. Does anyone have that?? If so please transcribe it for me if you can. Thanks

↳ Posted by b.maloney on January 5th, 2003.

The Dawn/The Miller’s Reel

The Dawn appears to be an Irish interpretation of an American tune called the Miller’s Reel, in Cole’s with the name of the composer (which I forget at the moment). The setting in Cole’s is played at least by Scottish fiddle player Karen Steven and to my ear is much finer musically than any of the various Irish settings of the the Dawn, which mostly differ slightly in the second part and are close to identical to the Miller’s Reel in the first.

Miller’s Reel

Re: The Dawn/ Miller’s Reel

In the second entry of this reel in Ryan’s Mammoth Collection (#343) it is called Miller’s Reel and credited to Zeke Backus. He “flourished” between 1840 and 1855. The following link shows he was a member of Christy’s Minstrels. https://tunearch.org/wiki/Biography:Zeke_Backus
Also see earlier info here https://thesession.org/discussions/47458#comment949605

↳ Posted by brailsford on July 31st, 2023.
